description: Blank sex is reported as its own group alongside the other sexes.

a.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), compute for each patient (by ID and sex) the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `IGA` − `IGM` per record, ignoring missing values. Also compute the mean of that IGA−IGM average across all patients, and divide each patient's IGA−IGM average by this overall mean. Then break the patients down by sex, keeping patients whose `SEX` is blank (an empty string) as a separate group of their own. For each sex, report the sex, the average of the patients' average PT, the average of their IGA−IGM averages, and the average of their ratios to the overall mean.
a.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L INNER JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), o AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS overall_mean FROM p) SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(p.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(p.avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(p.avg_diff / o.overall_mean) AS avg_ratio FROM p CROSS JOIN o GROUP BY p.SEX

c.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean. Blank sex is reported as its own group alongside the other sexes.
c.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, P.SEX AS SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) AS overall_mean FROM p) SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, AVG(p.avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(p.avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(p.avg_diff * 1.0 / m.overall_mean) AS avg_ratio FROM p CROSS JOIN m GROUP BY p.SEX

b.request: Inner-join Laboratory to Patient on ID, compute per-patient (ID, SEX) the average PT and the average of (IGA − IGM) ignoring NULLs, divide each patient's average IGA−IGM by the mean of those per-patient averages across all patients to get a ratio, then group by SEX (with blank/empty sex kept as its own group alongside the other sexes) and report for each sex the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio
b.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L INNER JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX), r AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_diff, avg_diff * 1.0 / (SELECT AVG(avg_diff) FROM p) AS ratio FROM p) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM r GROUP BY SEX

d.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean, with patients whose sex is blank reported as their own separate group alongside the other sexes.
d.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT P.ID AS ID, COALESCE(P.SEX, '') AS SEX, AVG(L.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(L.IGA - L.IGM) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = L.ID GROUP BY P.ID, COALESCE(P.SEX, '')), r AS (SELECT ID, SEX, avg_pt, avg_diff, avg_diff / AVG(avg_diff) OVER () AS ratio FROM p) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM r GROUP BY SEX
